title: Security — Secrets, API Key Rotation, Audit Logs, Guardrails

questions.question: What happens when Scrubber.scrub sees the same sensitive value twice?
options: It assigns a new placeholder each time
It removes the value without a placeholder
It reuses the stable placeholder stored in tokens
questions.explanation: _token_for first checks self.tokens, so repeated SSNs, emails, or phones receive the same kind-specific placeholder.

questions.question: Which entity types do the local regular expressions scrub?
options: Only model names and tenant IDs
SSNs, email addresses, and phone numbers
questions.explanation: main.py applies SSN, EMAIL, and PHONE patterns in sequence; other PII categories are outside this toy scrubber.

questions.question: Which privacy-preserving field does the audit example store instead of the raw prompt?
options: A short hash of the scrubbed prompt
questions.explanation: AuditEntry uses prompt_hash=hash_short(scrubbed), and audit_log_call serializes prompt_hash rather than the raw prompt.

questions.question: How long is the hexadecimal digest returned by hash_short?
questions.explanation: hash_short takes the SHA-256 hexadecimal string and slices the first 12 characters.

questions.question: What placeholder does a first-seen SSN receive from a fresh Scrubber?
questions.explanation: The SSN pattern calls _token_for("SSN", value); the counter starts at zero and formats the first token as [SSN_001].

questions.question: Which field is included in each JSON audit record for policy/guardrail outcomes?
questions.explanation: audit_log_call serializes guardrail_trips along with timestamp, tenant, hashes, token counts, cost, model, and user.
